issue.title: Add Download Queue Progress Bar to Coming Back Online Screen
issue.body: The Coming Back Online screen handles the moment a translator reconnects after working offline. While uploading completed work is the primary activity at reconnection, users may simultaneously have content downloading — newly assigned chapters or peer check material triggered by the reconnection event. This ticket adds a download progress section below the sync action buttons to surface that secondary activity without competing with the primary upload flow. ## Functional Requirements ### Download Progress Section - Position the download progress section below the Sync Now / Pause / Cancel buttons and above the "Upload over cellular" toggle. - Show the section only when the download queue contains at least one item; hide it entirely when the queue is empty. - Display a "Downloads" label with a `li:arrow-down-to-line` icon at the top of the section. Style it subdued — smaller text, lower visual weight than the upload section above. ### Download Progress Bar - Show a single horizontal aggregate progress bar reflecting all items currently in the download queue. - Display an item count label beneath the bar (e.g., "4 items remaining"). ### Download Queue List - List each queued download as a labeled row beneath the item count. - Tier 1 rows are labeled "Source Bible". `li:download` - Tier 2 rows are labeled with content type and book name (e.g., "Matthew — Audio", "Mark — Text"). `li:download` ### Manage Downloads Link - Display a tappable "Manage downloads" row (`li:chevron-right`) at the bottom of the Downloads section. - Tapping it navigates to the Prepare for Offline screen, where the translator can pause, resume, or cancel active downloads. - Style it subdued, consistent with the rest of the Downloads section. > **Note:** The progress bar is queue-based, not session-scoped. New items added while the screen is open (e.g., a newly assigned chapter pushed by a PM) are appended to the queue and the bar extends naturally — no reset. > **Note:** The bar may start at a non-zero fill if items were partially downloaded before the device went offline. This is intentional — do not reset partial progress on reconnection. --- ## Engineering context *(Added for implementation readiness. Product requirements above remain the source of truth.)* ### Product intent (summary) On the Coming Back Online / Sync screen, show a subdued Downloads section (aggregate bar, count, queue rows, Manage downloads link) when the download queue is non-empty — without competing with upload UI. ### Proposed technical approach 1. Depend on Sync page shell **#149** for layout slots; render Downloads below action controls and above cellular toggle (#146). 2. Subscribe to the same download queue used by #51/#52 (queue-based, not session-scoped; preserve partial progress). 3. Aggregate progress = completed bytes or items / total queued (define metric consistently). 4. “Manage downloads” → `navigate('PrepareForOffline', { projectId })` (project from active sync context or picker). ### Systems / modules / anchors - Sync route: `RootStackParamList.Sync` (typed; screen registration expected from #149 / PR #187) - Pending uploads hook pattern: `src/hooks/usePendingUploads.ts` — mirror as `useDownloadQueue` - Connectivity/prefs: `src/services/userPreferences.ts` (cellular toggle placement sibling) - Prepare for Offline: existing route in `AppNavigator.tsx` ### Implementation steps 1. Confirm #149 layout anchors for the Downloads slot. 2. Implement `useDownloadQueue` over shared inventory/queue. 3. Build Downloads section UI (label, bar, count, rows, manage link). 4. Hide section when queue empty; update live as items append. 5. Tests for visibility + aggregate math + navigation. ### Dependencies & prerequisites - **In-repo:** #149 (Sync layout), #51/#52 (download queue exists), #146 (toggle below). Upload engine #150 not required for this UI, but Sync page may be reached via coming-online flow tied to #150. - **External:** None beyond download assets already defined for offline prep. ### Edge cases & failure states - Queue item labels: Tier 1 always “Source Bible”; Tier 2 uses book + Audio/Text — confirm Tier 3 labeling (open question). - Project context missing for Manage downloads: fall back to Prepare for Offline picker. - Upload-complete but downloads remain: section still visible (`allComplete` must include downloads — #149 TODO). ### Testing & verification - Unit/component: empty hidden; non-empty shows; count label; manage navigation. - Manual: enqueue downloads, open Sync, see bar grow as items finish; append mid-session. ### Analytics / observability / migrations - None beyond queue telemetry from #51. ### Assumptions - Coming Back Online uses the same `Sync` screen as #149. - Progress is queue-global across projects unless product later scopes it. ### Open questions 1. How are Tier 3 rows labeled? 2. Aggregate bar: by item count or by bytes? 3. Which `projectId` is passed to Manage downloads when multiple projects have queued items? ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Downloads section only visible when queue length ≥ 1. - [ ] Placed below Sync action controls and above cellular toggle. - [ ] Aggregate progress bar + “N items remaining” + per-row labels per tier rules. - [ ] “Manage downloads” navigates to Prepare for Offline. - [ ] New queue items while screen open extend progress (no reset); partial prior progress preserved.

comments.body:
Findings from the returning online and synchronizing changes audit (#530, epic #526), Gaps 10 and 11. **Severity:** Low · **Launch blocker:** No.

**Confirmed on:** Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro, Android 10 (API 29), local debug build of `09ff2fd` (PR #559 head), `https://dev.api.fluent.bible` (scenarios I.25, I.26). The Downloads section itself passed: it shows below the controls with progress and "Manage downloads", and hides when the queue is empty.

**Gap 10 — Back from "Manage downloads" needs two taps.** Sync pushes Prepare for Offline with a `projectId` (`src/app/screens/SyncScreen.tsx:248-255`), which lands on the project screen above the picker. Back shows the Prepare for Offline picker; a second back returns to Sync.

**Gap 11 — The Sync page never reaches "All synced".** With uploads and downloads done it shows "Upload complete"; `deriveSyncPageStatus` never returns `allComplete` ("blocked on download-queue signal", `src/utils/deriveSyncPageStatus.ts:4-6`), the #149 TODO noted in this issue.

**Suggested extra AC:**

- [ ] One back from Prepare for Offline (opened via Manage downloads) returns to Sync.
- [ ] When uploads are complete and the download queue is empty, the Sync page shows "All synced" with `cloud-check` (#149).
- [ ] Unit tests for both; Android device QA (I.25, I.26).

Assessment: `docs/assessments/returning-online-and-sync/README.md` (PR #598)

**### Test Results **

* Downloads section is displayed correctly in the required position when downloads are available.
* Multiple downloads, aggregate progress, and remaining item count are displayed and updated correctly.
* Partial download progress is retained after reconnection without resetting.
* Upload and download activities work simultaneously, with upload remaining the primary flow.
* Downloads section is removed correctly once all downloads are completed.
* Manage Downloads navigation works, and pause/resume retains download progress.
* Cellular download settings work correctly for both ON and OFF conditions.
* App remains stable during network loss, download failure, large queues, and duplicate resources.

### Issues Identified

1. **Incorrect download labels:** Source Bible, Audio, Text, Translation Notes, and Translation Words are not displayed with the required labels.
2. **New downloads not reflected:** Newly added downloads are not automatically added to the queue, and the progress bar/UI does not update correctly.
3. **Cancel action not updating queue:** Cancelled downloads remain in the active queue, and the remaining item count is not updated correctly.
4. **Network recovery issue:** Downloads do not automatically resume after switching from a poor cellular connection to Wi-Fi; the user must manually start the download again.
